newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-ENGLAND MAKE RAPID START TO RUN CHASE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND MAKE RAPID START TO RUN CHASE.

text.p: England made a rapid start in their chase for 205 to win the first test against Zimbabwe on Sunday despite losing captain Mike Atherton cheaply.
The touring team, with a minimum of 37 overs to reach the target, were 36 for one off five overs at tea on the fifth and final day.
Atherton was bowled by paceman Henry Olonga in the fourth over for four, having been dropped in the gully off the same bowler in the previous over.
Opener Nick Knight was unbeaten on 16 at the interval and Alec Stewart was 12 not out, including a pull for six off Heath Streak, who took the new ball with Olonga.
Zimbabwe, 30 behind on first innings and 107 for five overnight, frustrated England until well into the second sesssion when they were all out for 234.

England made the best possible start by getting rid of nightwatchman Bryan Strang in the third over of the morning when he tried to heave the left-arm spin of Phil Tufnell over long on but succeeded only in hitting the ball straight up in the air toAlan Mullally at mid-on.
The touring side were then frustreated by a seventh wicket stand of 67 between 37-year-old test debutant Andy Waller (50) and all-rounder Guy Whittall.

Waller reached his half-century with his fifth four, having also hit two sixes in a stay of 106 deliveries. But three balls later Darren Gough found some extra bounce and Waller, trying to fend the ball down, succeeded only in edging it to Nick Knight at first slip.

Zimbabwe frustrated the tourists for a further 80 minutes in the afternoon session. Whittall shepherded the tail expertly and reached an excellent 50 before his first loose shot resulted in his downfall.
Whittall sliced a drive at Tufnell and was well caught by the diving Robert Croft in the covers. He made 56 off 184 balls with five fours and a six.
In the next over Chris Silverwood wrapped up the innings by having Olonga caught behind for a duck.
